tier_reason: Upgraded B to A: the independent kostya/jit-benchmarks suite publishes the benchmark code (<bench>/test.pyx and test.py), the exact build command and flags (tools/languages.rb: cython3 --embed, then gcc -O3 -march=native -fomit-frame-pointer -funroll-loops -g against libpython3.10), versions (Cython 0.29.30, Python 3.10.7, gcc 12.2.0 on the Ubuntu 22.10 base image) and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X).

corrections.baseline: CPython 3.10.7 (kostya/jit-benchmarks 'Python3' rows; Ubuntu 22.10 package, version listed in the README Versions table)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Cython 0.29.30 (Ubuntu cython3 package) `cython3 --embed test.pyx`, then gcc (Ubuntu 22.10 build-essential; the suite reports gcc 12.2.0) `-O3 -march=native -fomit-frame-pointer -funroll-loops -Wno-unused-result -g`, linked with -lpython3.10 (tools/languages.rb, GCC_FLAGS and the cython build_cmd).
corrections.claimed_speedup: Cython vs Python3 (CPython 3.10.7) best times, round 1 (2023-02-28): binarytrees 0.81 s vs 73.15 s; fannkuchredux 0.13 s vs 4.04 s; mandelbrot 0.43 s vs 37.52 s; nbody 0.56 s vs 53.72 s; matmul 0.39 s vs 22.73 s; spectralnorm 0.11 s vs 20.69 s; pidigits 1.73 s vs 6.17 s (about 31x to 188x on the numeric kernels, derived from page data). Small or no win on text tests: fasta 6.81 s vs 8.65 s, knucleotide 8.33 s vs 8.41 s; slower on regexdna 6.1 s vs 5.2 s; brainfuck 165.97 s vs CPython timing out above 190 s. No Cython row for brainfuck2 or revcomp.
corrections.caveats: The .pyx files are hand-typed Cython that is close to C: binarytrees allocates C structs with malloc/free while the CPython test.py builds Python class instances, and nbody uses cdef structs and extern math.h (Cythonized by Robert Bradshaw), so the numbers measure statically typed Cython, not unmodified Python compiled by Cython. Several CPython rows are a single run (binarytrees, nbody). Time is measured inside the program with time.time(), so process start-up and the 0.8-2.6 s Cython+gcc compile time are excluded. Versions are old (Cython 0.29.30, Python 3.10.7, round 1 dated 2023-02-28, not rerun). Cython's own README makes no numeric speed claim. Cython is a Python-to-C compiler rather than an interpreter.

notes: All numbers checked against the kostya/jit-benchmarks README rows; the record wrongly said the interpreter version and compiler flags were unstated (README Versions table and tools/languages.rb give them), which lifts the tier to A. Shortcomings to record: typed C-like .pyx vs idiomatic Python (different source per side), slower than CPython on regexdna and level on knucleotide, old 2023 versions, single CPython runs on the slowest rows.

tier_reason: First-party README headline ratios (34.6% faster than the LuaJIT interpreter, 185% faster than PUC Lua 5.1, geometric mean, i7-12700H) without compiler or flags for any of the three builds; taken alone this record is tier C.
notes: Same project as the already-verified https://github.com/luajit-remake/luajit-remake: the sillycross URL serves the luajit-remake/luajit-remake repository (Apache-2.0, 1.3k stars, last commit 2025-02-18 'implement dfg codegen log debug dump, fix bugs, add most of the lua tests'); the orchestrator has already recorded it as a duplicate. Record fields otherwise match the page.

tier_reason: The only numbers (txiki.js issue #301, posted 2022-07-25 by richarddd) predate the quickjs-ng fork (its LICENSE dates Ben Noordhuis's copyright from 2023), so they time Bellard's upstream qjs, not this repository; quickjs-ng's README and docs (diff.md lists opcode fusion, polymorphic inline caching, allocation and parse-speed work) give no numbers, so nothing measures this project against Node or any baseline.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No numbers for quickjs-ng itself. The linked issue (2022-07-25, before quickjs-ng existed) timed upstream QuickJS: `./qjs -e "console.log(1)"` 0.005 s total vs `node -e "console.log(1)"` 0.054 s total (about 11x less start-up time, derived from page data); txiki.js 0.115 s.
corrections.caveats: Evidence belongs to upstream Bellard QuickJS (already listed as https://github.com/bellard/quickjs): issue #301 was posted 2022-07-25, about a year before the quickjs-ng fork, and states no versions, hardware, OS or flags; it is one shell `time` run per runtime. Start-up only: sustained throughput is far below V8. In attractivechaos/plb2 (Apple M1, hyperfine) QuickJS 23-12-09 took nqueen 59.04 s and matmul 135.66 s vs Node 21.5.0 at 3.73 s and 2.88 s. quickjs-ng is measured slower than upstream QuickJS on the v8-v7 suite: quickjs-ng issue #1172 (opened 2025-09-28, still open) reports total score 992 vs 1326, and ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark's ubuntu CI run of 2026-10-05 shows quickjs-ng 647 vs quickjs 1217 vs node 40333 (CI runner, no CPU model).

notes: Downgraded C to D because the timed qjs cannot have been quickjs-ng (the fork did not exist in July 2022); the startup claim belongs to bellard/quickjs, and the orchestrator may prefer to fold this fork into that entry or keep it at D with the shortcoming 'no measurement of quickjs-ng; independent v8-v7 runs show it slower than upstream QuickJS'. Metadata checked: MIT, active (last commit 2026-10-06), 3.9k stars, self-described fork of Bellard's QuickJS.
